newsitem.title: POLAND: FLOOD GIVES POLISH RIGHT A BOOST - POLL.
newsitem.headline: FLOOD GIVES POLISH RIGHT A BOOST - POLL.

text.p: Poles would like to see a coalition of opposition parties in power after the September 21 parliamentary elections, the latest oppinion poll by the Pracownia Badan Spolecznych (PBS) pollster showed on Tuesday.

The survey, done on July 19-20, showed 20 percent of those polled would like to see a coalition of the right-wing Solidarity Election Action (AWS), Movement for Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) and centrist Union for Freedom (UW).
A previous poll by the independent PBS in June showed such a coalition was favoured by 18.7 percent of Poles.
The ruling coalition of the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and Peasant Party (PSL) got nine percent of votes in the July survey against 12.4 percent in June.

"The floods in southern Poland had a decisive influence on the change in voter preferences and offset the earlier negative perceptions of the AWS from infighting within that group," said Ryszard Gudyka, analyst at PBS.

Earlier this month Poland has been hit by severe floods, the worst in centuries, which inundated more than 6,000 square km killing 55, forcing tens of thousands out of their homes and causing wide-spread damage running in billions of dollars.
The opposition has heavily criticised the government for its handling of the crisis.

PBS also asked Poles who they expect, irrespectively of their preferences, is most likely to eventually win the elections and the results showed the front running SLD-PSL coalition eased to 17 percent in July from 19 percent in June.
However, expectations that the potential AWS-UW-ROP coalition would emerge victorious from the elections also eased to 14 percent in July from almost 17 percent in June.
Marginal gains were recorded by a potential coalition of the ruling SLD, the opposition Union for Freedom and the Labour Union (UP).
The number of Poles who would like to see such a team in power rose to 18 percent from 17.8 percent in June and their chances were seen as higher by 14 percent in July against 13.7 in June.

Preference for and chances of winning the September polls by a coalition of the right-wing AWS and populist Movement for Reconstruction of Poland or a team of AWS-ROP and the Peasants eased by between 0.5 and 1.8 point to five and seven percent respectively.
